thought.text: The php-fpm worker runs as `verein` (uid 1000), but files are root-owned since this environment runs as root. I'll fix ownership of the writable directories.

reasoning_content:
php-fpm worker runs as verein (uid 1000). Storage is owned by root because the repo files were checked out as root. Actually the mount is ./api:/var/www/html, so host permissions apply. Since we're running as root and copied .env etc., and the storage dirs are root:root 755, uid 1000 cannot write. 

The guide assumes the host user owns the files. In this benchmark, files are root-owned. This is an environment quirk. I need to make storage writable by uid 1000. That's a setup step. Let me chown storage/bootstrap cache to 1000.

Let me check whether the guide expects this. The tooling container runs commands as root (since we exec bash as root default). Actually the Dockerfile creates user verein and the working directory... but we exec as root by default. The composer install ran as root, creating root-owned files in api/. So mixed ownership. To make the API work, chown storage and bootstrap/cache to verein.

Let's do it.

action.command: cd /workspace && chown -R 1000:1000 api/storage api/bootstrap/cache && ls -ln api/storage | head -5 && echo "=== retry api ===" && curl -s -o /dev/null -w "api(3001): %{http_code}\n" --max-time 10 http://localhost:3001/ ; curl -s -o /dev/null -w "admin login: %{http_code}\n" --max-time 10 http://localhost:3001/admin/login

tool_call.name: terminal
tool_call.arguments: {"command": "cd /workspace && chown -R 1000:1000 api/storage api/bootstrap/cache && ls -ln api/storage | head -5 && echo \"=== retry api ===\" && curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"api(3001): %{http_code}\\n\" --max-time 10 http://localhost:3001/ ; curl -s -o /dev/null -w \"admin login: %{http_code}\\n\" --max-time 10 http://localhost:3001/admin/login", "security_risk": "MEDIUM", "summary": "Fix storage ownership and retest API"}

summary: Fix storage ownership and retest API
